subject: Design review: VPC collector auth, tracehooks, and evidence receipts
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <abarnes@finserv.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finserv.com
Date: 2026-11-18T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Design review: VPC collector auth, tracehooks, and evidence receipts

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. We’re starting a POC to ship VPC telemetry (logs + metrics + traces) from our enclave to Redwood’s private forwarder in our VPC. Two items compliance is focused on and I wanted your design opinion before we lock the PO: 

1) Authentication/egress: we need short-lived credentials for the forwarder that rotate automatically and are auditable. Long-lived keys are a no-go.
2) Evidence receipts / delivery proofs: for audit we need signed receipts guaranteeing the data bundle was received and a tamper-evident hash chain for batches (so our SIEM can reconcile ingestion).

Questions for the review call next week:
- Recommended auth model (mTLS vs ephemeral signed tokens vs short-lived API creds) when the forwarder lives in customer-managed VPCs
- A minimal evidence/receipt format that works across Splunk/QRadar/SIEM ingestion and doesn’t leak PII
- Tracehook placement: sidecar collector (per pod) vs centralized forwarder — tradeoffs for trace continuity and span sampling

Attached a short sketch of our current collector flow; happy to share sample logs if helpful.

Can you loop in anyone from your compliance or product team I should meet?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Barnes
Head of Observability Engineering, FinServ Corp

Attachments: collector_auth_flow.png
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Barnes <abarnes@finserv.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design review: VPC collector auth, tracehooks, and evidence receipts

Alex —

Appreciate the context. High-level proposals below; I’ve included acceptance criteria and a short rollout path so your security and compliance teams have something concrete to review. I also attached a proposed evidence receipt spec and a scrubbing checklist for PII.

Option A — mTLS + short-lived client certs (recommended for on-prem/VPC):
- Provision a customer-managed PKI or our managed issuance (we sign a leaf cert for the forwarder).
- Cert TTL: 24h (rotate via ACME-style automated renewal).
- Enforcement: TLS mutual auth at the forwarder ingress with CN mapped to tenant id.
- Pros: strong crypto, no bearer-token leakage; easy for network egress policies.
- Cons: PKI ops for some customers; initial bootstrap needs secure channel.

Option B — Ephemeral signed tokens + session binding:
- Short-lived JWTs (5–15m) signed by customer KMS or Redwood’s signing service; tokens contain a nonce + forwarder fingerprint.
- Use TLS for transport and bind token to client certificate fingerprint to reduce token replay.
- Pros: simpler for some cloud customers; works with existing token rotation systems.

Evidence & receipts (common design):
- Batch-level HMAC (sha256) over canonicalized bundle (logs.jsonl, meta.json, last-offset) using customer key or tenant-specific HMAC secret.
- Redwood returns a signed receipt with: receipt_id, batch_hash, received_at (ISO8601), ingestion_offsets, and an operator signature (Ed25519).
- Receipt is returned synchronously for small batches or asynchronously via a signed webhook (customer chooses).
- Receipt format: JSON-LD stub (see attached evidence_receipt_spec.md).
- Audit chain: store receipts immutable with sequence numbers; optionally publish a daily Merkle root to a customer-accessible endpoint for external verification.

Tracehook placement guidance:
- Sidecar collectors provide best fidelity (span continuity, local sampling) but increase surface area (per-pod certs/tokens).
- Centralized forwarder reduces auth surface (single forwarder identity) and simplifies batching/receipt generation, at a cost of partial span context loss if pod-to-forwarder connectivity is flaky.
- Hybrid approach: sidecar -> local aggregator (per node) -> central forwarder. Aggregator issues per-node ephemeral creds to central forwarder.

Acceptance criteria for POC:
- End-to-end: collector authenticates, sends batch, receives signed receipt within SLA (<=30s for small batches).
- Receipt contains batch_hash and Ed25519 signature verifiable with Redwood’s public key.
- Sample logs (attached sample-logset.json) pass scrub rules and ingestion mapping into your SPL/QRadar feed.
- Trace continuity: 95% of sampled traces maintain root-span id when flow goes via aggregator.

Next steps / ask from you:
1) Which auth option does FinServ prefer (A/B/hybrid)?
2) Compliance wishlist — any additional fields required on the receipt for audit?
3) Can your security team review the attached spec and we’ll schedule a 45-minute call on Monday or Tuesday PST?

I’ll bring Marissa (supporting acceptance tests) and Kim (legal/compliance gateway questions).

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_receipt_spec.md, sample-logset.json
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Barnes <abarnes@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design review: VPC collector auth, tracehooks, and evidence receipts

Rishi / Alex —

A few compliance points we need to confirm before the POC kickoff: 

1) Key custody: if FinServ wants us to sign receipts with Ed25519 using Redwood keys, legal requires an SLA addendum stating key usage scope and rotation cadence. If FinServ prefers customer-managed keys (recommended), we need an API hook for public-key upload and a KMS-key-id reference.

2) Evidence retention: what is the retention window for receipts and raw ingest metadata? Compliance typically wants 7 years for specific FIN logs; we should surface configurable retention per-tenant so we don’t default to a single policy.

3) PII scrub validation: please confirm the scrub rules we’ll use for POC and whether we should run a blind hashing step for any customer identifiers prior to batch_hash calculation.

Operational asks: Marissa — can your team own the POC runbook (sample data, acceptance scripts)? I’ll coordinate legal addendum language once Alex confirms key custody approach.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Barnes <abarnes@finserv.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finserv.com
Date: 2026-11-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design review: VPC collector auth, tracehooks, and evidence receipts

Rishi / Kim / Marissa —

Thanks — this is very helpful. FinServ prefers customer-managed keys + mTLS for the forwarder ingress (Option A with customer PKI). We’ll provide a test KMS key and a short-lived cert issuance endpoint for the POC. For retention: we need a configurable per-tenant retention up to 7 years for certain audit logs.

We’ll accept the proposed receipt format; I’ll have security@finserv.com review the attached spec and flag any mandatory fields. Let’s lock Monday 2026-11-22 10:00am PST for the call.
